batchName: Empire: The Year of Four Emperors and the Flavians (AD 69-96) - Latin words
chapterName: Empire: The Year of Four Emperors and the Flavians (AD 69-96)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What did the Romans mean by decimatio, the punishment Galba used?
options: Putting to death one soldier in ten
Sending a tenth of the army home
questions.explanation: Galba used it on the survivors of a legion of former sailors.
questions.sourceQuote: decimation (*decimatio*), the ancient punishment in which one soldier in ten was put to death.

questions.question: What does pecunia non olet mean?
questions.explanation: Tradition links it to Vespasian’s tax on urine from public toilets.

questions.question: What is the Amphitheatrum Flavium better known as?
questions.explanation: Vespasian began it and Titus opened it in AD 80.
questions.sourceQuote: the Flavian Amphitheatre (*Amphitheatrum Flavium*), better known as the Colosseum.

questions.question: Titus made his dead father a divus. What was that?
questions.explanation: Vespasian, like Augustus and Claudius before him, was declared a god.
questions.sourceQuote: He made his dead father a god (*divus*).

questions.question: What was the Templum Pacis that Vespasian built?
options: A temple to the Flavian family
questions.explanation: It was part of his campaign presenting himself as a bringer of peace.
questions.sourceQuote: He built a Temple of Peace (*Templum Pacis*)

questions.question: Vitellius took the office of Pontifex Maximus. What was it?
questions.explanation: He took it on the anniversary of the Battle of the Allia, an unlucky day.
questions.sourceQuote: He took the office of chief priest (*Pontifex Maximus*)

questions.question: In AD 68 the Senate declared Nero a hostis. What is a hostis?
questions.explanation: The next day Nero took his own life.

questions.question: After Domitian’s murder the Senate imposed damnatio memoriae. What was it?
questions.explanation: Senatorial historians then portrayed him as a cruel tyrant.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate condemned his memory (*damnatio memoriae*)
